theorem: For every ring length L>=3, U,tau>0, B>=0 and unknown |lambda|<=B, the periodic spin-1/2 model H=U sum_i|n_i-n_(i+1)|-(lambda/L^2)M at beta=tau L^2 has Z=Tr([[1,q],[qz,z]]^L), q=exp(-tau U L^2), z=exp(tau lambda); its mixed (0<M<L) mass is at most 2^L q^2, and the parameter-independent two-label map M=0 -> |0^L>, M>0 -> |1^L> has whole-state trace error exactly that mixed mass. For B>0, the minimax no-message error tends 1/2 while the two-label error tends 0.
proof_evidence: Self-contained transfer-matrix and domain-wall proof in outputs/research/spin_statistical/cycle2/leaves/leaf04_local_no_go/RESULT.txt sections 1-3. Standard-library exact Fraction replay for L=3..8 in work/programmes/spin_statistical/cycle2/leaves/leaf04_local_no_go/exact_phase_separation_check.py and exact_phase_separation_check.json verifies finite instances only.
inputs_costs: Supplied L,U,tau,ring,field window B and interaction; lambda is unknown and not queried. Encoder scans/measures O(L) local bits and retains one bit; decoder prepares a product phase using O(L) one-site operations. Gibbs input generation and hardware noise are excluded. Full M archive costs log2(L+1) bits and is exact; the two-label archive has error <=exp(L log 2-2 tau U L^2).
baseline_falsifier: Strongest equally informed baseline is the exact L+1-sector channel. A mixed ring configuration with fewer than two walls, transfer-matrix mismatch, or archive error above p_mix falsifies the result. The finite rational replay tests the partition, two-wall coefficient, tail, and archive at L=3..8; general proof is analytic.
sources: N20 scope audited from work/astra_prior/cards/N20-critical-quartic.txt:1-5. Primary background: Fannes-Kossakowski-Verbeure (1991) https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01053756; Davies (1979) https://doi.org/10.1017/S0305004100056383; Koma-Nachtergaele (1995/1997) https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9512120; Nachtergaele-Starr (2000/2001) https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0009002. These sources are context, not proof premises.

theorem: The universal claim that every finite-range stable spin interaction at beta=tau L^2 and detuning lambda/L^2 inherits an occupation-count tail decaying uniformly as exp(-c d^3+O(d^2)) is false. In the attractive domain-wall ring above, at lambda=0, Z=(1+q)^L+(1-q)^L->2 and P(M>=d)>=P(M=L)=1/Z->1/2 for every 1<=d<=L.
proof_evidence: Exact transfer matrix and pure-phase event in RESULT.txt sections 1-3; rational finite configurations and all thresholds replayed for L=3..8 in the scratch script/output.
inputs_costs: Counterexample uses range-one bounded interactions with pair attraction -2U and a supplied field window containing zero; no acquired data or parameter query. It targets the raw count tail, not the XX theorem or N20 theorem.
baseline_falsifier: A single explicit instance in the stated universal class with a nonvanishing tail refutes universality. The result does not refute a narrower theorem limited to nonzero hopping and a continuous z=2 one-magnon saturation transition.
